detailed_rationale:
Poly Medicure is India's leading domestic medical-devices manufacturer (IV cannulas, infusion/transfusion sets, dialysis and other disposables), with a meaningful export franchise that has historically supported a premium multiple versus generic pharma/healthcare names. The quant sheet shows a quality score of only 35 despite a strong 3yr revenue CAGR (18.9%) and growth score of 69 -- the FY26 print explains why. Q4 FY26 revenue rose to Rs.535cr (from Rs.494cr in Q3) but net profit actually fell to Rs.65cr (from Rs.71cr) as operating margin compressed to ~21% versus a ~27% recent average. More importantly, working-capital days roughly doubled over the year to 249 days by year-end (debtor days 77->103, inventory days ~265), and borrowings rose to Rs.354cr. Revenue is growing, but cash conversion is deteriorating and profit is not keeping pace -- a classic earnings-quality caution rather than a clean compounding story.

ROE of 13.6% and ROCE of 17.3% are respectable but middling for the 54x earnings the stock commands (value_score 38.4, among the lower scores in this cohort). Balance sheet leverage itself is low (D/E 0.11, interest coverage ~24.6x) so there is no solvency concern, but the combination of margin compression, ballooning receivables/inventory, and TTM profit growth turning slightly negative argues for treating the recent 18-19% CAGR as backward-looking rather than a reliable run-rate. Medtech import-substitution and PLI tailwinds remain real structural positives, but near-term execution has clearly softened.

Net: a genuine quality franchise trading at a valuation that assumes the deceleration is temporary. The quant Hold is the right call; nothing here rises to a Sell-worthy thesis, but nothing here argues for paying up either.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is already Hold (46.3/3yr). Fundamentals confirm rather than override that call: real business quality (medtech leadership, low leverage) is offset by a genuinely weaker recent quarter (margin compression, working-capital stress, profit growth turning negative) that does not support the 54x multiple re-rating higher. No basis to rescue to Hold (already Hold) and no basis for Sell under the asymmetric-override rule even if conviction were bearish -- it isn't; this is a monitor-the-working-capital-trend situation, not a broken business.
summary: Poly Medicure is a strong domestic medical-devices franchise, but the latest quarter showed profit falling even as revenue grew, with receivables and inventory both building up faster than sales. The valuation already prices in continued strong growth, so we see this as a name to hold and watch rather than one to add to at current levels.
positive_para: Poly Medicure is the clearest domestic leader in medical disposables (IV cannulas, infusion sets, dialysis products) with a genuine export franchise, benefiting from import-substitution and PLI incentives in a structurally growing category (rising hospital admissions, chronic disease burden, domestic manufacturing push). Balance sheet leverage is low (D/E 0.11, interest coverage ~24.6x), five-year sales and profit CAGRs of ~19% show a long real compounding track record, and the business operates in a defensive, non-discretionary end-market.
negative_para: The most recent quarter is the tell: net profit fell sequentially even as revenue rose, operating margin compressed roughly 6 points versus the recent average, and working-capital days nearly doubled over the year (debtor days 77->103, inventory ~265 days), funded partly by higher borrowings (Rs.354cr). TTM profit growth has turned slightly negative. At ~54x earnings, the market is still pricing continued high-teens growth with stable margins; if the working-capital deterioration reflects channel stuffing or slowing collections rather than one-off timing, the multiple has further to compress before it is attractive.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~54x trailing earnings the multiple is pricing sustained mid-to-high-teens growth with stable-to-improving margins. The current quarter shows margin compression and a profit decline despite revenue growth, so the business is not currently clearing what the multiple implies. Fair-to-rich, not cheap; the long-term compounding story is real but the multiple leaves no room for the working-capital/margin wobble to persist.
